title: Derivative certificate and inverse-generator presentation for a unit binomial
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq1$ an integer, $a\in R$ with $a(n\cdot1_R)=1$, and $u\in R^\times$. Put $f=T^n-u\in R[T]$, $B=R[T]/(f)$ and $C=R[T,Y]/(f,Yf'-1)$, with their quotient $R$-algebra structures [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; here $f'=nT^{n-1}$ is the formal derivative. Let $t\in B$ and $x,y\in C$ be the respective classes of $T$ and of $T,Y$. Write $v$ for the image of $u^{-1}$ in $B$ and $\bar a$ for the image of $a$. Then
$$t^n=\bar u,\qquad t(vt^{n-1})=1,\qquad f'(t)h=1,\quad h=\bar a(vt^{n-1})^{n-1}.$$
There are mutually inverse $R$-algebra homomorphisms $\alpha:C\to B$ and $\beta:B\to C$ specified by
$$\alpha(x)=t,\quad\alpha(y)=h,\quad\beta(t)=x,\quad\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}_B,\quad\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_C.$$
In particular the canonical structure maps are identified by this $R$-algebra isomorphism. The assertions include the zero ring and $n=1$.

Agent-extracted algebra isomorphism underlying that assertion.

proof.text: The quotient map has kernel $(f)$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], so $t^n=\bar u$. Put $s=vt^{n-1}$. Since $n\geq1$, $ts=vt^n=v\bar u=1$. All these equations use only the quotient ring operations and $u^{-1}u=1$.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), affine calculation that n and T^(n-1) are invertible in B; explicit elementary expansion by Q79.

proof.text: Using the coefficient description in [def-weil-polynomial-ring], formal differentiation sends $\sum c_iT^i$ to $\sum_{i\geq1}ic_iT^{i-1}$, hence $f\prime=nT^{n-1}$. Commutativity and $ts=1$ give $f\prime(t)h=(n\bar a)t^{n-1}s^{n-1}=(ts)^{n-1}=1$. Here $n\bar a=1$ is the image of the assumed equation $an=1$.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), affine calculation that n and T^(n-1) are invertible in B; explicit elementary expansion by Q79.

proof.text: By evaluation in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $T\mapsto t$, $Y\mapsto h$ defines an $R$-algebra homomorphism $E:R[T,Y]\to B$. Both $f$ and $Yf\prime-1$ map to zero. Every element of their generated ideal is $Pf+Q(Yf\prime-1)$ and therefore maps to zero. Thus $[P]\mapsto E(P)$ is independent of the representative modulo that ideal, preserves sums, products and constants, and defines $\alpha:C\to B$ with the specified generator values.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), affine calculation that n and T^(n-1) are invertible in B; explicit elementary expansion by Q79.

proof.text: The relation $f(x)=0$ holds in $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Evaluation $T\mapsto x$ from [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] (one variable) kills every multiple of $f$. Consequently $[P]\mapsto P(x)$ is a well-defined $R$-algebra map $\beta:B\to C$, with $\beta(t)=x$.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), affine calculation that n and T^(n-1) are invertible in B; explicit elementary expansion by Q79.

proof.text: The composite $\alpha\beta$ fixes $t$ and all images of $R$. Every class of $B$ is represented by a finite sum $\sum r_it^i$, so it fixes every class. For the other composite put $d=f\prime(x)$ and $k=\beta(h)$. Applying $\beta$ to $f\prime(t)h=1$ gives $dk=1$, whereas the defining relation of $C$ gives $yd=1$. Hence $y=y(dk)=(yd)k=k$, so $\beta\alpha$ fixes $y$ as well as $x$ and constants. Every class of $C$ is a finite sum $\sum r_{ij}x^iy^j$; thus this composite also is the identity.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), affine calculation that n and T^(n-1) are invertible in B; explicit elementary expansion by Q79.

proof.text: Both maps fix the image of every $r\in R$, so the inverse maps identify the structure maps as asserted in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. When $n=1$, $s=v$, $h=\bar a=1$ and $f\prime=1$, so the same computations apply with exponent zero. In the zero ring every displayed identity still holds, with $0=1$; the proof uses neither cancellation by a nonunit nor a nonzero hypothesis.
